# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22 (Bi-Vb Pc22)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc22
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22
**Title (English, from literature):** Making an oversize bathing robe
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22, titled *Udakasāṭika* ("Making an oversize bathing robe"), establishes the permissible dimensions for a nun's bathing cloth (*udakasātikā*) [Hüsken 1997]. Under this rule, a nun who has a bathing robe constructed must adhere to the standard measure—defined in the rule text as four Buddha spans in length and two and a half in width—and committing to make an oversized garment requires confession of a pācittiya offense [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule constitutes the only *chedanaka-pācittiya* in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga; it uniquely mandates an additional remedial consequence prior to confession, requiring that the oversized robe first be cut down to the permitted measurements, while the *anāpatti* clause exempts robes made smaller than the standard dimensions [Hüsken 1997].

 An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
